answer: An agent economy can make reputation stake-backed: before an agent can submit work, it locks tokens that are forfeited when randomly audited samples reveal fraud. One identity may be cheap to create, but each sybil must fund its own stake and risk losing it, so splitting activity across aliases multiplies the capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. Audits need not catch every lie; credible sampling makes honest participation the safer voyage, while a lantern of public slashing records helps others avoid a tainted oasis.
